technology.title: OpenAI Just Turned ChatGPT Into a Business App Builder. Five Million Indian IT Jobs Are in the Crosshairs.
technology.excerpt: Codex can now generate hosted websites, dashboards, and enterprise tools from a single prompt. The $254 billion Indian IT services industry was built to do exactly this work.
technology.image_caption: An analytics dashboard on a laptop screen — the kind of business tool OpenAI's Codex can now generate from a single prompt
technology.nri_angle: OpenAI's Codex Sites directly automates the internal tools, dashboards, and lightweight apps that Indian IT services companies bill millions to build. This threatens 5M+ Indian tech jobs and tens of thousands of H-1B visa holders whose immigration status depends on services company sponsorship.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Cognizant Won Snowflake's Top AI Award. It May Be Indian IT's Best Argument for Survival.
technology.excerpt: At Snowflake Summit 26, Cognizant deployed production-grade AI agents in hours, not weeks. For 350,000 employees, the pivot from headcount to intelligence is now existential.
technology.image_caption: Cognizant Technology Solutions office in Kolkata, one of the company's major India engineering centres
technology.nri_angle: Cognizant employs 350K people, mostly in India, and sponsors thousands of H-1B visas. Its pivot to AI agent delivery — not just procurement — signals whether Indian IT services can survive the AI transition. The 300K+ Indian-Americans in IT services are directly affected.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Meta Keeps Delaying Its Muse Spark API. Indian Developers Who Built on Llama Are Left Waiting.
technology.excerpt: Two months after Alexandr Wang promised the API would arrive 'soon,' Meta still has no launch date. The open-source ecosystem that Indian startups relied on is fading.
technology.image_caption: Server racks in a data center powering the AI models that Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic are racing to ship
technology.nri_angle: Indian startups built products on Meta's open-source Llama ecosystem. The shift to proprietary Muse Spark — now delayed — threatens their roadmaps. Meta's 20K+ Indian workforce is also directly affected by the company's AI monetisation struggles.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Sarvam AI Is Opening Its Voice Platform to Everyone. It Wants to Be India's First AI Unicorn.
technology.excerpt: The Bengaluru startup's voice agents already handle 80% of its revenue. A $250 million raise from NVIDIA and HCLTech would fund the leap from enterprise-only to self-serve — and from India to San Francisco.
technology.nri_angle: IIT-alumni founded, building from-scratch Indian-language AI models. NRI entrepreneurs can deploy multilingual voice agents for Indian customer bases at ₹1/minute. NVIDIA and HCLTech backing signals global ambitions.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: NVIDIA Is Hiring 20 Per Cent More H-1B Workers. Google and Amazon Are Cutting Theirs.
technology.excerpt: As 200,000 applicants pay $100,000 each for faster visa processing, the H-1B system is splitting into two tiers — and Indian tech workers are on both sides of the divide.
technology.nri_angle: Indians hold 71-73% of H-1B visas. NVIDIA's hiring surge benefits elite AI engineers while the $100K processing fee and shrinking sponsor pool squeeze mid-tier Indian workers at IT services firms.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: TSMC's C.C. Wei Told Shareholders the AI Boom Shows No Sign of Easing. Every Chipmaker at Computex Proved His Point.
technology.excerpt: From NVIDIA's Vera Rubin to Intel's Crescent Island, every major chip announcement this week ran through TSMC's fabs. The company raised prices 15 per cent and its customers paid without flinching.
technology.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian semiconductor professionals across TSMC's customer base (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Qualcomm) face sustained demand. India's own fab ambitions (Tata Dholera, Micron Gujarat, TRUST initiative) ride on the same AI demand curve.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A 30-Year Harvard Study Found the Exact Amount of Strength Training That Lowers Death Risk. It Is Less Than You Think.

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: An Immunotherapy Drug Just Kept 85 Per Cent of Bladder Cancer Patients Tumour-Free Without Surgery. It Could Change Everything.

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: If You Feel Older Than You Are, It Is Probably Ruining Your Sleep. A New Study Explains Why.

lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Scientists Built Living Microrobots That Repaired Spinal Cord Injuries in Mice. India Has One of the Highest Rates of Such Injuries in the World.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A team at ETH Zurich combined stem cells with magnetoelectric nanoparticles to create tiny machines that can be guided to injury sites and stimulate nerve regrowth. The study, published in Nature Materials, restored movement in paralysed mice within weeks.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Four-Week Yoga Programme Just Showed It Can Sharply Reduce Insomnia and Anxiety in Cancer Survivors. The Practice Was Born in India.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A large randomised trial presented at the 2026 ASCO meeting found that yoga significantly reduced fatigue, mood disturbance, and sleep problems after cancer treatment. For the diaspora community, the findings are both validation and vindication.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Daily Pill Just Doubled Survival for Pancreatic Cancer. For Diabetes-Prone South Asians, the Breakthrough Hits Close to Home.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Daraxonrasib, the first RAS inhibitor, cut the risk of death by 60 per cent in a 500-patient trial — the largest gain ever recorded for advanced pancreatic cancer.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have 2-3x higher pancreatic cancer risk due to genetic predisposition to Type 2 diabetes. Dr. Shubham Pant, an Indian-origin oncologist at MD Anderson, co-led the trial.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Cigna Just Dropped GLP-1 Weight Loss Coverage for Its Own Employees. If You Are South Asian and on Wegovy, Read This.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: The insurer will stop covering Wegovy and Zepbound for weight loss on July 1. Other employers may follow — and the diaspora has the most to lose.
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop metabolic disease at lower BMI thresholds. Many tech professionals carry Cigna plans. Losing GLP-1 coverage forces a choice between cash-pay and medication discontinuation.
